hook: Artificial intelligence just unlocked 461 years of hidden British maritime history.

sections.voiceover: Artificial intelligence just unlocked 461 years of hidden British maritime history.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up shot of delicate handwritten 16th-century port books resting on a wooden archival desk.
b_roll: 16th-century handwritten port book pages in an archive

sections.voiceover: Lambert secured a 2.86 million euro European Research Council Advanced Grant to fund it.
sections.visual_cue: Medium shot of researchers operating a digital scanner next to stacks of historical documents.
b_roll: University of Southampton research laboratory archival scanning setup
sections.animation_cue: Slow zoom in on document text

sections.voiceover: Except the Uncharted Maritime Worlds project needed 5 years to pull it off.
sections.visual_cue: Extreme close-up panning across fading ink script written on aged parchment.
b_roll: Fading ink on 16th century manuscript parchment

sections.voiceover: Researchers transformed the port books into an interactive map revealing 461 years of trade. Historians mapped centuries of lost trade routes starting from the Elizabethan Era.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of a modern computer display showing a glowing digital interactive maritime map of Britain.
b_roll: Interactive digital map of British maritime trade routes on computer screen
sections.animation_cue: Zoom out revealing full digital map interface

sections.voiceover: Historians compiled a first-of-its-kind online interactive map using that artificial intelligence data.
